ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Three 1-liter flasks are connected to a 3-liter flask by valves. The 3-liter flask is evacuated to start and the entire system is at 298K. The first flask contains helium, the second argon, and the third krypton. The pressure of the argon is 633 torr. The amounts of gas are proportional to their representations in the flasks. If all the valves to the center flask are opened, what will the pressure of the system be? Assume the connections have negligible volume.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three small 1 L flasks, labeled He, Ar, and Kr respectively, and connected to the large central flask through Valve 1, Valve 2, and Valve 3. Inside each small flask, small dots are used to represent the amount of gas; according to the proportion represented by the dots in the figure, the total amount of gas in the three small flasks is equal to 3 times the amount of gas in the argon flask. Reasoning: The initial pressure of argon in the 1 L flask is 633 torr, so the amount of substance of argon is proportional to 633 torr × 1 L. The total amount of gas is 3 times the amount of argon. After all valves are opened, the gas occupies the three 1 L flasks plus the central 3 L flask, with a total volume of 6 L. The temperature remains unchanged, therefore P_final = (3 × 633 torr × 1 L) / 6 L = 316.5 torr, taking approximately 316 torr according to the problem's answer.

raw_record.question_text: Three 1-liter flasks are connected to a 3-liter flask by valves. The 3-liter flask is evacuated to start and the entire system is at 298K. The first flask contains helium, the second argon, and the third krypton. The pressure of the argon is 633 torr. The amounts of gas are proportional to their representations in the flasks. If all the valves to the center flask are opened, what will the pressure of the system be? Assume the connections have negligible volume.

method.method_draft: Use the image dot counts to infer that the total gas amount equals 3 times the amount of argon gas. From the text, argon is initially in a 1-L flask at 633 torr, the center 3-L flask is evacuated, and all three 1-L flasks plus the 3-L center flask become one 6-L system after opening the valves. Treat the total gas as 3 argon-flask equivalents, so P_final = (3 × 633 torr × 1 L) / 6 L ≈ 316 torr.

method.method_draft: Assign relative initial pressures from the visual counts: P_He = 633(N_He/N_Ar), P_Ar = 633, and P_Kr = 633(N_Kr/N_Ar), since all three outer flasks are 1 L at the same temperature. The bracketed visual ratio sum is 3, giving P_total ≈ 316 torr.
